key_insight: Human-in-the-loop prompting with SAM (Hi-Seg) can substantially improve pulmonary nodule segmentation by letting people iteratively guide the model with trial-and-error and semantic reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This approach could reduce clinician annotation burden and support scalable, safer medical image labeling workflows, including use by junior trainees or trained non-medical annotators.
method: Built Hi-Seg on the Segment Anything Model for pulmonary nodule segmentation.
Humans refined prompts iteratively to steer the model toward better masks.
Evaluated performance across multiple annotator groups in a collaborative workflow.
evidence_signal: Using chest CT scans from 1,179 patients across 12 centers, Hi-Seg achieved a mean Dice score of nearly 85% and outperformed 5 deep learning models and 13 SAM variants.
watch_item: Performance may depend on prompt quality and user training, so real-world deployment needs careful validation, supervision, and workflow integration.
paper_title: Human and AI collaboration for pulmonary nodule segmentation
